answer: Wait-Time Identity Ladder. Each new agent identity must wait out a mandatory dormancy period before its votes or transactions count, and the wait grows on a spiral for each identity created from the same network origin or device fingerprint. An attacker renting many identities pays in wall-clock delay, not money: the hundredth puppet waits weeks while honest single identities ripple through instantly. Small operators absorb the cost; farms cannot, since each fake node adds latency. Residual risk from slow, patient attackers remains a walnut to crack later.
